newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- State Council sets up leading group on bankruptcy
- Commentary calls for regulations on bankruptcy, encouraging mergers and re-employment of workers

- Commentary repudiates Dalai Lama's activities over past decades as disrupting and hindering development of Tibetan Buddhism, says Dalai Lama has stood as biggest obstacle to building normal order of Tibetan Buddhism.
BEIJING DAILY
- Retail price inflation in Beijing rose 5.5 percent in the first quarter of this year over same period of 1996.
CHINA YOUTH DAILY
- State Education Commission issues regulation to encourage university graduates to work in remote, poverty-stricken areas.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China consumer associations nationwide receive total of 105,318 complaints from consumers in first quarter, up 15.5 percent from year-ago
- Agricultural Bank of China Luzhou branch in Sichuan province, sells securities outlet to J & A Securties
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Xinjiang foreign trade volume hits $319.713 million in first quarter, up 54.16 percent year-on-year
- Southern Yunnan provice tea exports hit 10,617 tonnes in 1996, earns $15 milion, but decling quality troubles tea industry
CHINA BUSINESS DAILY
- China completes construction of large wharf for oil exports in Dalian, can handle 3.85 million tones of oil production and 120,000 tonnes of LPG annually
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- Hainan plans to sell its largest bankrupt firm with debts of 361.98 million yuan
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- About 40 percent of China's breweries make losses
MARKET DAILY
- State Planning Commission and State Industrial and Commercial Bureau issue circular banning unauthorised dealing in sedan cars
CHINA DAILY
- China will achieve this year's target of $310 billion in foreign trade volume, but over-optimistism should be avoided, a vice-minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation says
- Ceremony marks 10th anniversary of founding of Tibet Development Fund, China's first non-governmental charity organisation in Qinghai-Tibet Plateau.
